glossary.Fc receptor: A receptor on immune cells that grips the tail end of an antibody, holding IgE on mast cells.
glossary.Cross-links: When one allergen binds two neighbouring IgE molecules at once, triggering the mast cell to release its contents.
glossary.Hypersensitivity: An exaggerated or inappropriate immune response that damages the body's own tissues.
glossary.Vasodilation: Widening of blood vessels, causing redness, warmth and a fall in blood pressure.
glossary.Vascular permeability: How leaky blood vessel walls are; when raised, fluid escapes into tissues and causes swelling.
glossary.Smooth muscle: Involuntary muscle in airways, gut and vessels; contraction in airways narrows them.
glossary.Mediators: Chemical messengers such as histamine released by immune cells that produce inflammation.
glossary.Eczema: Chronic itchy, dry, inflamed skin condition, common in atopic people.
glossary.Hay fever: Seasonal allergic rhinitis caused by pollen, giving sneezing, itchy eyes and a runny nose.
glossary.Asthma: Chronic airway inflammation with reversible narrowing, causing wheeze, cough and breathlessness.
glossary.Wheezing: A high-pitched whistling sound on breathing out caused by narrowed airways.
glossary.Failure to thrive: Older term for a child not gaining weight or growing as expected.
glossary.Hypoallergenic formula: Infant milk with proteins broken down or replaced so it is unlikely to trigger allergy.
glossary.Exclusively breastfed: An infant fed only breast milk, with no formula or solids.
glossary.Elimination: Removing a suspected food from the diet to see whether symptoms improve.
glossary.Reintroduction: Bringing the food back after elimination; symptoms returning confirms the allergy.
glossary.Multi-system: Affecting several body systems at once, for example skin, gut and breathing.
glossary.Latex: Natural rubber used in gloves and catheters, a common cause of contact allergy.
glossary.Histamine control: A positive control drop in skin prick testing that should always produce a wheal.
glossary.False positive: A test result that says positive when the condition is not actually present.
glossary.Total IgE: The overall level of IgE antibody in the blood, not specific to one allergen.
glossary.T-cell-mediated: An immune reaction driven by T lymphocytes rather than antibodies, typically slower in onset.
glossary.Delayed hypersensitivity: A Type IV reaction appearing hours to days after exposure, driven by T cells.
glossary.Bronchodilators: Inhaled drugs, such as salbutamol, that relax airway muscle and open the airways.
glossary.Inhaled steroids: Corticosteroids breathed into the lungs to reduce airway inflammation in asthma.
glossary.IM: Intramuscular: an injection given into a muscle.
glossary.IV fluid bolus: A quick infusion of fluid into a vein to raise blood pressure.
glossary.Alpha-agonist: A drug stimulating alpha-adrenergic receptors, causing blood vessels to constrict.
glossary.Receptor downregulation: Cells reduce the number of receptors after constant stimulation, so a drug works less well.
glossary.Rebound vasodilation: Vessels widen more than before once a constricting drug wears off, worsening congestion.
glossary.Vasoconstriction: Narrowing of blood vessels, reducing blood flow and swelling.
glossary.Topical: Applied directly to the surface where it is needed, such as skin, eye or nose.
glossary.Intranasal: Given into the nose, usually as a spray.
glossary.Bronchospasm: Sudden tightening of airway smooth muscle, narrowing the airways and causing wheeze.
glossary.Calcium supplements: Tablets of calcium to replace dietary calcium lost when dairy is cut out.
glossary.NICE CG116: The NICE guideline on diagnosing and assessing food allergy in children and young people under 19.
glossary.Insect bite: A sting or bite that can trigger a local or systemic allergic reaction.
